rows.05:b74c: Went to a fair in the next town
rows.05:b770:
He skipped school and went to the next town.
It was fair season back then.
Okura wasn't the only one cutting class to go have fun there, either.
Me included, as a matter of fact.
The fair runs at night too, but goofing off isn't any fun unless you break the rules a little, right?
Who I went with, I'll leave to your imagination.
Anyway, I was shocked when I spotted Okura.{p}
rows.05:bd3c:
Maybe he fell wrong, but the knife plunged right into Okura's gut.
Right then, a voice spoke up behind me.
"Oh my, oh my. You failed, didn't you?"
I turned around, and there was the old man from the stall.
He was looking down at Okura with a thin smirk.
"Still, a soul is a soul, no matter whose it is... It's more than enough to pay for these tarot cards."{p}
rows.05:be6c:
The old man waved the cards around like he was showing them off.
Okura was staring at them, bitter, but he didn't even have the strength left to reach out.
"And here I was, finally willing to sell. But in that state, it doesn't look like you'll be using them.
What about your friend there?
How about a deck of tarot cards that'll do whatever you want?
Right now, you can have them in exchange for Okura's soul."
The old man said that and looked at me.
Tarot cards you could make do whatever you wanted.
So Okura's playing cards had been the same kind of thing.{p}What would you do in a spot like that?
rows.05:cd08:
Okura turned to face me.
His eyes were glittering.
"Well, you've seen it now. Can't be helped.
I'm going to trade these contracts to a devil and get even better at gambling.
Not just at school, either. I'm going to play for way bigger stakes!"
My body wouldn't move.
It was like something had me pinned in place.{p}
rows.05:d724:
He'd cut the pads of his fingers with the knife and was feeding them his blood.
Tiny women's heads were sucking on all five of Okura's fingers.
It was a grotesque sight.
Half of each face was a pure-white skull, right?
And yet the other half was smiling happily, like the blood tasted that good.
Their eyes were narrowed and half rolled back, showing the whites.
"These things can't live unless they eat people.
I'm out of time.
I need the souls of fifty-three people, no matter what!"
That's what Okura was screaming.
Maybe I was caught in those women's spell, because I couldn't move a single step.{p}
rows.05:db78:
"Stop it!
I'll feed you, like I promised!
As long as I've got these contracts, you'll never run short of food!
The food isn't m......"
Okura couldn't get away anymore.{p}
rows.05:dd94:
I don't remember what happened after that.
I killed Okura.
Even now, I can still see it.
...What happened to Okura after that, you ask?
Strangely enough, the bloodbath I saw in that classroom was gone without a trace, all cleaned up as if nothing had ever happened.
Okura was listed as missing.
He wasn't at home either.
He just vanished on everyone, out of nowhere.
Though I'm the only one who knows the real reason.{p}
rows.05:df24:
...But you know, lately I've been thinking.
Maybe it was all just an illusion.
At least let me believe that much.
Otherwise, I'm a murderer.
I don't know what those women were.
I bet those cards are their home.
And normally, they hide by plastering themselves flat on the backs of the cards.
Not that I have any idea where the cards or the contracts are now.
But what's going to happen to everyone who signed a contract back then?
How do you even go about eating a soul?
Did Okura vanish from this world without even leaving a body because his soul got eaten?
If that really happened, and those women ran off with everybody's contracts...
I just can't stop thinking about it.
I mean, I'm one of the people who signed a contract too.
If those women are hunting down everyone who signed, then someday I'll...
Shindo had been staring at the floor, but suddenly he looked up.{p}
rows.05:e270:
"Please, {a}!
Play me at cards, will you?
Whoever loses takes responsibility for the contract. That's the deal!"
{f:What the heck is that|What is that supposed to be}?
{f:I|I} was dumbfounded.
It was crazy that he seriously believed that, and the deal didn't do anything for {f:me|me} either.
This was {f:ridiculous|absurd}.
But Shindo {f:seemed|looked} genuinely terrified.
Somehow, I kind of felt sorry for him.{p}What should I do?
rows.05:e8d0:
Shindo was so crushed it was almost pitiful.
Maybe he was more sensitive than he looked.
But {f:I|I} had no intention of playing again just for his sake.
Sorry, Shindo, but I {f:had to|needed to} move things along.{p}"Well then, the sixth story, please."{p}
rows.05:ed14:
But there were more of them.
What should I {f:do|do}?
Should I tell Shindo?
But what {f:would I do|would I do} if that made him angry and he lunged at me?
{f:I|I} agonized over it.
{f:They must have taken|It seems they took} my hesitation for awkwardness.
Someone spoke up in {f:my|my} place.{p}"Well... time for the last story."
{f:I|I}'d missed my chance, so all I could do was keep silent......{p}
